1. Whether Reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see the judgment?

2. To be referred to the Reporter or not?

         

Justice J.D. Kapoor, President (Oral)

1. There is no dispute that the appellant purchased a new computer from the respondent against consideration of Rs. 31,500/-. It developed defects right from the beginning. According to the appellant the defect was that of mother board. But according to the respondent there was defect in the hard disc. Since neither the defect was removed nor the computer was replaced, the appellant filed the instant complaint before the District Forum for replacement of computer or refund of price thereof.

2. Vide impugned order dated 08.04.03, the District Forum dismissed the complaint firstly on the ground that there was discrepancy in the date of purchase of the computer and secondly that the respondent visited the premises of the appellant alongwith the engineer to get the computer repaired as early as possible but due to non-cooperation of the appellant he failed to repair it. Feeling aggrieved the appellant has preferred this appeal.

3. Respondent is present before us. He states that there was some defect in the hard disc which he was ready to rectify.

The appellant has accepted this version of the respondent but is aggrieved of the failure of the respondent to rectify the defect.

Respondent stated that he had told the appellant that it would take one month to remove the defect but the appellant asked for hand to hand replacement which the company does not allow.

4. Any goods or articles having any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or implied, or is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods renders the goods as a defective goods and if during the warranty period the defects are not removed, the seller is required to compensate the consumer. To say that the company does not permit hand to hand replacement of the defective parts and therefore he had asked for one months time to repair it amounts to deficiency in service. No consumer can be deprived of the use of the computer for one month because of its defect as it results in financial loss as well as mental harassment to the consumer.

5. However, taking over all view of the matter and the version of the respondent who is merely a dealer of the company, we deem that lump sum compensation of Rs. 5,000/- which shall be inclusive of the cost of litigation or in the alternative replacement of the hard disc by a new hard disc within one week from the date of receipt of this order shall meet the ends of justice. If respondent chooses to replace the hard disc he shall also pay Rs. 1,000/- as cost of the proceedings.

6. A copy of this order as per the statutory requirements be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to Record room.

7. Announced on 10th day of August, 2007.

     

(Justice J.D. Kapoor) President       (Rumnita Mittal) Member     ysc
